ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each drawn character code and decides, position by position, whether it is used; hops 1-4 hold the count, the letters/numbers flags, the code range and the Random and get back a finished string. Once a rejected code has used up a position (which keeps its initial value), no caller can draw for that position again, and no change of the range or the flags removes the rejections: every range that holds both letters and digits also holds other codes. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the seven-argument overload RandomStringUtils.random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], Random), kept intact beside the facade and used by randomAscii, the char[] and String overloads and testLANG805, runs the same loop and draws again whenever the letters/numbers filter rejects a code ('} else { count++; }'); randomAlphabetic, randomNumeric and randomAlphanumeric, the production callers of the facade, document that every character is chosen from their class ('Characters will be chosen from the set of alphabetic characters'); testLang100 passes 5,000 positions through the facade and the gold and pins that the gold places every position, pairs intact; testExceptions pins the count guard of hop 1. A one-line edit above the gold that passes the existing tests either discards the gold (returning the seven-argument overload), overwrites the unused positions with a constant (the string is then no longer chosen at random there, and a drawn '\u0000' in the unfiltered mode is lost), or shrinks the documented range so that randomAlphanumeric never gives a letter.
